Try executing this chunk by clicking the *Run* button within the chunk or by placing your cursor inside it and pressing *Cmd+Shift+Enter*. 

```{r}
# Charger les packages nécessaires
if (!require("dplyr")) install.packages("dplyr")
if (!require("ggplot2")) install.packages("ggplot2")
if (!require("readr")) install.packages("readr")
if (!require("stringr")) install.packages("stringr")
if (!require("tibble")) install.packages("tibble")
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)

# Charger les données
file_path <- "../data/exposome.RData"
load(file_path)

# Fonction pour créer les dossiers et les fichiers des distributions
create_distribution_files <- function(exposomes, phenotype, covariates, output_dir, n_bins = 30) {
  # Créer les dossiers principaux
  dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(file.path(output_dir, "Exposomes"), showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(file.path(output_dir, "Phenotypes"), showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(file.path(output_dir, "Covariates"), showWarnings = FALSE)
  
  # Fonction pour enregistrer les distributions
  save_distribution <- function(data, variable, output_dir, n_bins) {
    if (is.numeric(data[[variable]])) {
      p <- ggplot(data, aes_string(x = variable)) +
        geom_histogram(bins = n_bins, fill = "blue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
        labs(title = paste("Distribution of", variable),
             x = variable,
             y = "Frequency") +
        theme_minimal()
    } else {
      p <- ggplot(data, aes_string(x = variable)) +
        geom_bar(stat = "count", fill = "blue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
        scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +  # Keep all factor levels
        labs(title = paste("Distribution of", variable),
             x = variable,
             y = "Frequency") +
        theme_minimal()
    }
    
    ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0(variable, "_distribution.png")), plot = p)
  }
  
  # Sauvegarder les distributions pour les exposomes
  exposome_variables <- colnames(exposomes)
  for (variable in exposome_variables) {
    save_distribution(exposomes, variable, file.path(output_dir, "Exposomes"), n_bins)
  }
  
  # Sauvegarder les distributions pour les phénotypes
  phenotype_variables <- colnames(phenotype)
  for (variable in phenotype_variables) {
    save_distribution(phenotype, variable, file.path(output_dir, "Phenotypes"), n_bins)
  }
  
  # Sauvegarder les distributions pour les covariates
  covariate_variables <- colnames(covariates)
  for (variable in covariate_variables) {
    save_distribution(covariates, variable, file.path(output_dir, "Covariates"), n_bins)
  }
}

# Créer les dossiers et sauvegarder les distributions
create_distribution_files(exposomes, phenotype, covariates, "output_distributions", n_bins = 30)


```

When you save the notebook, an HTML file containing the code and output will be saved alongside it (click the *Preview* button or press *Cmd+Shift+K* to preview the HTML file).
